query: Across Type of Traveller and Class, which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating?

per_column.name: crew_warmth_engagement
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated categories (high_warmth / low_warmth_robotic / mixed) that capture a review theme distinct from the numeric rating and can be segmented against it.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_problem
per_column.rationale: Clean binary flag with a healthy 750/150 split; easy to group on and compare rating distributions, though it partially overlaps the existing Seat Comfort column.

per_column.name: meal_quality_consistency
per_column.rationale: Distinct, interpretable food-theme categories; the ~171 NULLs still leave three well-populated groups for comparison.

per_column.name: premium_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Value/price perception theme with clear categories, well-suited to segmentation across Class; some conceptual overlap with Value For Money but adds a themed angle.

per_column.name: cost_cutting_perception
per_column.rationale: Interpretable cutback-perception categories, well distributed; a meaningful theme to correlate with rating, though it overlaps semantically with premium_value_perception.

per_column.name: communication_responsiveness_failure
per_column.rationale: Binary service-failure flag with a usable 672/228 split; groupable and interpretable against rating.

per_column.name: ground_staff_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Clear ordered/nominal categories capturing a distinct service touchpoint; well-populated groups enable meaningful comparison.

per_column.name: aircraft_cabin_freshness
per_column.rationale: Interpretable cabin-age theme; the 450 NULLs weaken it, but the remaining three categories are still comparable against rating.

per_column.name: post_covid_service_change
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories; however the dominant 'no_comparison_made' (471) plus a tiny 'service_improved' (35) make some contrasts thin, though still usable.

judge.rationale: All added columns are external, associational review-theme variables expressed as interpretable, well-separated categorical or binary segments rather than opaque scores, directly supporting exploration of which themes correlate with higher/lower Overall Rating across Type of Traveller and Class. They are theme-decomposed and do not merely restate the numeric focus. Deductions: several columns overlap conceptually (premium_value_perception vs. cost_cutting_perception; seat_comfort_problem/meal_quality partly echo existing sub-ratings), and a few carry heavy NULL or near-constant dominant categories (aircraft_cabin_freshness at 450 NULLs, post_covid_service_change dominated by 'no_comparison_made'), which limits comparison power for those specific fields. As a set, however, the columns strongly enable discovery of interpretable relationships.
